fact: NatCA states that in November 2024 Sierra Leone and Guinea signed an agreement to interconnect their national internet backbone networks.

SOGEB (Guinea) and Leoncom (Sierra Leone) signed an interconnection agreement in Conakry to link their national fibre networks at Pamelap on the border, with initial capacity of 42.5 Gbps and plans for 100 Gbps by 2026; the document gives no date for the signing, so its published date is used.

Guinea's telecoms ministry says its operational cross-border interconnection with Sierra Leone, one of four with neighbours, was achieved in 2025, after the two countries' November 2024 agreement to join their national backbones.

Sierra Leone's minister Salima Monorma Bah and Guinea's minister Rose Pola Pricemou signed a framework agreement in Freetown on 22 November 2024 that includes interconnecting the two countries' national internet backbones, per Agence Ecofin.
WACREN, supported by European Commission co-funded AfricaConnect projects, says Sierra Leone joins its research and education network backbone.

Sierra Leone's communications ministry reports that it and Guinea signed a framework agreement on 22 November 2024 covering infrastructure sharing and the linking of fibre networks, to be overseen by regulators NaTCA and ARPT and a joint commission.
